triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: unclear: the pre-fix formula returned 0 whenever permanent_ineligibility_applies and otherwise tested the two-year tier before the one-year tier, while the post-fix formula tests one-year first, two-year second, and has no permanent gate; 7 USC 2015(b)(1) sets tiers (i) 1 year, (ii) 2 years, (iii) permanent without stating precedence, so neither ordering is clearly the source's, and on overlapping triggers the post-fix version arguably reads worse (a first determination that is also the first controlled-substance trading finding now yields 1 year although clause (ii)(II) specifies 2 years, and a permanently disqualified person can now report a non-zero 'nonpermanent' period).
triage.triage_notes: This is the only substantive formula change in the entire commit (verified by YAML-parsing every changed module pre and post and comparing rules modulo whitespace). Pre: 'if permanent_ineligibility_applies: 0 else: if two_year_ineligibility_applies: two_year_ineligibility_period_years else: if one_year_ineligibility_applies: one_year_ineligibility_period_years else: 0'. Post: 'if one_year_ineligibility_applies: one_year_ineligibility_period_years else: if two_year_ineligibility_applies: two_year_ineligibility_period_years else: 0'. Everything else in this module is cosmetic: per-rule source strings, blank-line separators, parenthesis reindentation in two_year_ineligibility_applies and permanent_ineligibility_applies (semantically identical), and one added proof atom (kind: parameter) on this rule. Commit body is empty and prep_commit found no PR (pr: null), so no maintainer statement explains the reorder; the subject frames the commit as a metadata regeneration, which suggests encoder churn rather than a deliberate fidelity fix. Provision read through the pinned corpus release (us/statute/7/2015): tiers (i)/(ii)/(iii) are listed in that textual order with no precedence rule. Companion test statutes/7/2015/b/1.test.yaml was edited but its cases do not discriminate between the two encodings (no case has two tiers firing at once); its edits flip household_would_receive_increased_benefits inputs and rename two cases. Follow-up: commit b3801ee4e ('Regenerate validated US RuleSpec encodings') later deleted nonpermanent_ineligibility_period_years entirely, replacing it with a Judgment rule permanently_ineligible, so the post-fix state here was itself superseded. Recommend a reviewer treat this as candidate churn/possible regression rather than a confirmed fidelity correction.
triage.verifier_justification: The only meaning-bearing edit in the module is the `nonpermanent_ineligibility_period_years` branch structure; every other change is the trimmed summary heading, added `source:` strings, an added proof atom, blank lines, and re-indent/re-parenthesization of formulas whose operands are byte-identical (same 10 rules, same entities, dtypes, periods, effective dates, inputs and outputs). For this to be a fidelity correction the post-fix ordering would have to be the source's ordering, but 7 USC 2015(b)(1) as resolved through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-07-13) states tiers (i) 1 year, (ii) 2 years, (iii) permanently with no precedence rule, and the one overlap it does settle cuts the other way: (ii)(II) assigns 2 years to "the first occasion of a finding ... of the trading of a controlled substance ... for benefits", which the post-fix now answers with 1 year whenever that finding is also the first determination, while the pre-fix answered 2. Dropping the permanent gate likewise makes a rule named "nonpermanent" report 1 or 2 years during a permanent disqualification, which is not closer to the source either. The commit message is a bare regeneration subject ("Regenerate SNAP work rules with source metadata", empty body, no PR), and all four companion tests evaluate identically under the pre- and post-fix formulas, so nothing in the record treats the old branch order as wrong — this reads as regeneration drift, not a corrected defect.
triage.verifier_notes: Refutes the first reader's "polarity_or_logic / unclear" in the direction of not_a_defect rather than confirmed. Key checks: (1) `two_year_ineligibility_applies` keeps its second disjunct `federal_state_or_local_court_first_found_trading_controlled_substance_for_benefits` unconditioned on an IPV determination (only reflowed in this diff), so it genuinely overlaps `one_year_ineligibility_applies` = `intentional_program_violation_determination and first_occasion_of_any_such_determination`; on that overlap pre gave 2, post gives 1, against (ii)(II). (2) The companion test file changed only test names and two household-rule inputs/expectations (an input flip, not a formula change); no test covers an overlapping-trigger case, and the permanent test has both one-year and two-year not_holds so it yields 0 under either formula. This is why it cannot be graded mechanical either: the formula's semantics did move, it just did not move toward the source. If a reviewer wants to keep it in the corpus at all, the defensible framing would be a regression introduced by regeneration, not a defect corrected by it. Sources read: diff 002.diff; full pre d66e787a76:statutes/7/2015/b/1.yaml and post c36a7900e0:statutes/7/2015/b/1.yaml; statute text via resolve_provision.py citation us/statute/7/2015, corpus commit 612d20ca43, text sha256 0367aadc0d.
